fields.h1: Build an Employee Engagement Survey From Question to Action
fields.hero_description: Describe your teams and what you need to learn. Emergent builds the questions, anonymous team results, driver analysis and manager dashboards, in a database you own.
fields.features_heading: What an Engagement Survey Needs to Work
fields.features_subheading: An employee engagement survey measures how committed people are to their work and employer, and what drives that number.
fields.feature_1:
Questions grouped by engagement driver

Core items on pride, intent to stay, advocacy and extra effort come first. Driver sections on managers, growth, recognition and workload follow. Reword any item with one sentence.
fields.feature_2:
Anonymity thresholds you set

No dashboard shows results for a group with fewer than five answers, and comments carry no names or emails. The first screen states that rule before anyone answers a question.
fields.feature_3:
Engagement index and eNPS per team

Each team gets an engagement index from the core items and an eNPS from one 0-10 question, shown next to the company result and the team's own score from the last cycle.
fields.feature_4:
Driver analysis that ranks what to fix

Each team's driver scores are correlated with its engagement index. The items that move it most rise to the top of the manager's view, ahead of the averages for all 40 questions.
fields.feature_5:
Org data synced from your HRIS

Department, location, tenure and manager sync from your HRIS, such as BambooHR or Workday. Results split along those lines without a single demographic question in the survey.
fields.feature_6:
Action plans the next survey checks

Managers log the actions they agreed with their team after each cycle. The next survey asks whether each one landed, and the answers appear beside the action they refer to.

fields.usecase_heading: Engagement Surveys to Build This Week
fields.tab_content_1:
A yearly census that names each team's focus driver

A 40-question survey goes to all 600 employees for two weeks, and reminders reach only people who have not answered. Teams with fewer than five answers stay hidden but still count in the totals. Each manager sees their team's index and eNPS beside the driver that moves it most, then logs actions.
fields.tab_content_2:
Frontline staff answer on a phone in two minutes

Store and warehouse staff without a company email scan a QR code in the break room and answer 12 questions in English or Spanish. The code tags each response to its site, and the site manager sees nothing until that site has five answers.
fields.tab_content_3:
Find the teams a reorg has unsettled

Six weeks after a reorg, affected teams answer a short survey on role clarity and trust in leadership, plus the core intent-to-stay item. Each team's intent to stay is compared with its last census, and a drop of 10 points or more alerts the HR business partner in Slack.
fields.tab_content_4:
Track eNPS every quarter without survey fatigue

Each quarter, people answer the eNPS recommend question and one open question on what would raise their score. A live dashboard tracks the company eNPS quarter over quarter. In Q3 the score rose from +12 to +18, and 400 comments fell into four themes led by growth.

fields.howto_title: How to Create an Engagement Survey
fields.howto_description: An engagement survey is worth what managers do with its results. These steps start with the decisions you want to make and end with the first action plan.
fields.howto_step_1_title: 01 Decide what you will act on
fields.howto_step_1_des: Start with the decisions the results should inform, such as whether engineering attrition after a hiring freeze is a manager problem or a workload problem. Every question should map to one of them. Items nobody acts on teach people that answering changes nothing.
fields.howto_step_2_des: Use four to six core items for engagement itself and never reword them between cycles. A changed item breaks the comparison with last year. Add driver sections for the areas from step one, written as single statements on the same 1-5 agreement scale.
fields.howto_step_3_des: Set the smallest group whose results anyone can see, such as five answers. Below that floor, the group's scores never appear. Then decide whether managers read comments word for word or as themes. In small teams, themes are safer, because a turn of phrase can identify its writer.
fields.howto_step_4_des: Write it out in plain English: who gets it, which questions, the scale, the anonymity rule and the reminder schedule. Emergent turns that into a working survey with its own response table and team dashboards. Later changes take one more message.
fields.howto_step_5_des: Tell people why you are asking and the date results come back. Keep the survey open for two weeks and remind only those who have not answered. A live response rate by department shows managers where a nudge is needed.
fields.howto_step_6_title: 06 Read the drivers, not the averages
fields.howto_step_6_des: Start with each team's two headline numbers, then the drivers most tied to them. A low item that does not move engagement can wait. A middling one that does is where the first action belongs.
fields.howto_step_7_des: Share company and team results within a month. Each manager then agrees a short list of actions with their team and logs it on the dashboard. People keep answering when the next survey asks about those actions by name.

scope.evidence: H1 'Build an Employee Engagement Survey From Question to Action', meta title 'Employee Engagement Survey You Can Act On' and hero ('the questions, anonymous team results, driver analysis and manager dashboards') state the whole job: questions, results, drivers, action. No sibling topic.

intent.evidence: Top 10 is Gallup Q12, question lists (Culture Amp, DecisionWise), a SurveyMonkey template and vendor directories (SHRM, Perceptyx). The page gives ten example items (faq 5), a template answer (faq 2), a vendor table plus faq 8 'How do I compare employee engagement survey vendors?', a 7-step how-to, a definition as faq 1 and features_subheading for the AI Overview, and all 5 on-topic PAA questions. P2: Gallup Q12 ranks #1 and is never mentioned; one line naming it (e.g. in faq 5 or faq 7) would serve searchers who arrive from it.

specificity.evidence: Buyer vocabulary throughout: 'engagement index', 'eNPS from one 0-10 question', 'HR business partner in Slack', 'BambooHR or Workday', 'store and warehouse staff without a company email scan a QR code in the break room'; table uses the employee variant 'Pulse and annual surveys, anonymous reporting, and manager dashboards, as code you own'.

openers.evidence: Every paragraph opens on a full sentence that says what happens: feature_2 'No dashboard shows results for a group with fewer than five answers...', feature_6 'Managers log the actions they agreed with their team after each cycle.', tab_content_3 'Six weeks after a reorg, affected teams answer a short survey...', faq 9 'Not exactly.', faq 2 'Yes.'

craft.evidence: No 'which/that is what' tails (searched all fields); one ', so' ending, in alt tab_image_3 ('fell from 81 to 67, so the HR business partner gets a Slack alert'), within the QC allowance; two 'from X to Y' ranges with real values (tab_content_4 'from +12 to +18', alt 3 'from 81 to 67') plus the H1; sentences carry one idea each. 'two or three' now appears once (faq 4).

voice.evidence: Recycled sentence, the same class cycle 3 failed ('stay hidden but still count in the totals'): tab_content_1 'goes to all 600 employees for two weeks, and reminders reach only people who have not answered' is repeated as howto_step_5_des 'Keep the survey open for two weeks and remind only those who have not answered' (the mockup's 'Keep it open two weeks, remind only people who have not answered' is a prompt and may stay). Keep the reminder rule once on the page (tab 1) and give step 5 something it lacks, e.g. what the launch message says. Summary sentence (HUB_RULES 2b 'no summary sentence restating the paragraph'): howto_description 'These steps start with the decisions you want to make and end with the first action plan.' signposts the list below it and repeats the H1's 'From Question to Action'; cut it or replace it with a fact (how long a census cycle takes end to end). Searched every field for other recycled pairs: 'the driver that moves it most' (tab_content_1) / 'The items that move it most' (feature_4) is a near echo; vary one of them.

truth.evidence: The page contradicts its own FAQ 1. faq 1 now says 'In a confidential survey the system knows who answered and can split results by team, but no manager sees one person's answers. An anonymous survey stores no identity at all.' That definition is correct (it matches how Culture Amp and Qualtrics use the terms), but by it the survey this page sells is confidential, not anonymous: tab_content_1 'reminders reach only people who have not answered', howto_step_5_des 'remind only those who have not answered' and the mockup annualCensus 'remind only people who have not answered' all require the system to know who answered, and feature_5 'Department, location, tenure and manager sync from your HRIS... Results split along those lines' is identity-linked splitting. Yet the page promises anonymity in: meta_description 'anonymous team results', hero_description 'Emergent builds the questions, anonymous team results, driver analysis and manager dashboards', hero_prompt 'with anonymous results by team'. Fix: call the census-style survey confidential in those three fields (e.g. 'confidential team results'), and in faq 1 say which this page builds (the census in tab 1 is confidential; the QR survey in tab 2 collects no identity, so it is anonymous) so the definition and the product agree. 'Anonymity thresholds' (feature_2 heading), 'anonymity rule(s)' (howto_step_3_title, howto_step_4_des, prompt_chip_2) are the industry term for the minimum-group rule and may stay. Also faq 1 implies only a confidential survey 'can split results by team', while tab_content_2 splits an identity-free survey by site through per-site QR codes; reword so the anonymous case can still split by a tag. Verified and holding: no census figure is quoted anywhere in the copy now (faq 10 no longer cites 412/72/+16); tab 1 image 412 of 600 = 118+84+66+141+3 and 69% = 412/600; weighted index (118x76+84x69+66x58+141x77)/409 = 72.0 and eNPS 6481/409 = +15.8 are not drawn or quoted; Platform 81 to 67 = -14 (Mobile -4, Data -1, Design +1, Search -2 all correct); 142+118+86+54 = 400; +12 to +18 agrees across tab 4, uc-4 and the cover. One anonymity rule everywhere: 'fewer than five answers' (feature_2, tab_content_1, mockup, howto_step_3_des 'such as five answers', tab_content_2 'until that site has five answers'), with hidden answers counted in totals stated once (tab_content_1) and drawn (Legal 3 in 412). Claims map to the ledger (prompt-build, database-owned, code-export, api-connect, alerts, realtime, free-start, no-caps).

distinct.evidence: Own territory per the watch-list (commitment and eNPS drivers): census, frontline QR, post-reorg and quarterly eNPS scenes share nothing with /customer-satisfaction; satisfaction is handed off in faq 9 ('Contentment with pay and role is the job of an employee satisfaction survey') and pulse in faq 10. P2: tab 4 'Quarterly Check-In' (two questions every quarter) is what most vendors call a pulse survey; the H3 avoids the sibling primary and faq 10 draws the line at a monthly rhythm, so accepted, but the planned pulse-survey page must not reuse a quarterly eNPS scene.

faq.evidence: Exactly 10 on-topic questions, each answered in its first sentence; 5 from PAA, the rest from secondaries (template, vendors, opinion survey, feedback survey); hub link in item 2 ('AI survey builder'), sibling links read naturally ('an employee satisfaction survey', 'a pulse survey'). faq 5 lists exactly ten items. No answer restates the body (searched against features, tabs and steps). The faq 1 confidential/anonymous wording is a truth fix, listed under truth.

images.evidence: uc-4 tells a different outcome from tab_content_4. The hero is a Slack post '# people-leaders / Growth is the top theme / 142 of 400 comments in Q3 / Open theme' (alt: 'with growth flagged to people leaders as the top theme'), but tab_content_4 and the quarterlyCheckIn mockup never mention posting to people leaders or Slack: the copy says 'A live dashboard tracks the company eNPS quarter over quarter... 400 comments fell into four themes led by growth.' Either add the step to the copy and mockup (e.g. 'and the top theme posts to the people leaders' Slack channel') or make the hero the dashboard moment. Also 'tracks the company eNPS quarter over quarter' is drawn only as '+18, Q3, up from +12'; acceptable. Other tabs match: uc-1 Legal 'Hidden, under 5 answers' with its 3 counted in '412 of 600', Support 'Log actions'; uc-2 'Question 3 of 12', English/Spanish, Store 214 '5 answered' unlocked, Warehouse 3 hidden; uc-3 Platform -14 against 'Alert when a team drops 10 points or more' in #hr-partners; cover '+18, up from +12 in Q2' agrees with tab 4. One hero per panel, text readable, no collisions.
